parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, border, facility or custody regime for visitors is documented, and acceptance signals are strong: constitutional anti-discrimination protection, supreme/regional court floors for recognition, a 2024 transfemicide law in the capital, large Pride, and a Zapotec third-gender tradition with community acceptance. Against this, the combined regime shows documented police extortion/abuse and nightlife targeting, killings of trans people in 2023-24, regional-commission impunity warnings, and a 2024 finding that progressive legislation is rarely enforced fairly or uniformly. Raw transfemicide counts have no denominator and cannot establish a trans-specific rate. The operative risk is therefore societal/police violence with thin recourse, not state imprisonment for identity.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police corruption, extortion and abuse of transvestites documented; nightlife districts targeted since 2007. No sourced trans-prisoner housing, placement or segregation data.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Capital allowed same-sex conjugal visits from 2007 under 2003 anti-discrimination law; no trans-specific custody protection documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch for residents amplifies discrimination, but no documented visitor detention pathway; status for visitor custody is uncertain.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: Separate states vary on recognition, but no visitor facility rule is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Street prostitution illegal in some jurisdictions; no trans-specific presentation offence documented. Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 1871.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional Article 1 amended 2011 prohibits gender/sexual-preference discrimination; 2003 anti-discrimination law; capital criminalised transfemicide in 2024, entry into force and prosecutions not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal protections coexist with documented uneven enforcement and police abuse, limiting their traveller-facing effect.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-dependent visitor or guardian rule documented; family-rejection figures are LGBTQ-wide, undated and excluded as prevalence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans woman found in river Aug 2023; at least three trans people killed early 2024 including activist shot in capital; regional commission warned impunity may reach alarming levels. Raw counts 593 (2008-Sep 2021) and 52 (Oct 2022-Sep 2023) lack denominators/baseline.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Regional commission in 2024 urged prevention, punishment and gender-respecting investigation; protests and LGBTQ outrage followed killings.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are recorded both as abusers/extortionists and as the expected responders; no documented pattern of prosecutions for attackers.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2024 analysis: progressive LGBTQ legislation rarely enforced fairly/uniformly, rights rarely enjoyed in practice, not evidence of safety from violence including murder/torture.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Supreme court 2017 and regional court 2018 establish recognition as protected right; anti-discrimination council created 2003; national hate-crime protocol actions declared 2019.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident recognition patchwork is a climate signal only for visitors; border, facility, custody and care outcomes remain undocumented/uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that protest/harassment occurs but courts dismissed charges and review found misconduct. Here no case shows remedies working for a visitor, and impunity warnings plus rarely-enforced legislation make recourse thinner, so lower than 0.65.

Similar in sporadic harassment, slow remedies and uncertainty. Here there is stronger acceptance infrastructure, no documented transit ejection or administrative-hold system for visitors, and no universal-exposure measure, so higher than 0.55.

0.75 has equality protection, police review and prosecution of attackers when evidence is clear. Here institutional failure is explicitly documented and police abuse is a pattern, with no documented prosecution record, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no documented traveller-facing state exposure at entry, facilities, care or custody, and no criminalisation of trans identity, with strong formal and cultural acceptance signals. The documented operative exposure is street and police-level: extortion/abuse, nightlife targeting, isolated killings, and impunity, combined with enforcement that rarely works uniformly. Absence of border/facility/custody evidence is not safety, but also not a tier-1 exposure. That places the case below 0.65 working-remedy anchors and above 0.55 universal-exposure anchors.
